analysis:
Examined the SSDWriteBehind.swift head text and the test patch. The change adds a prepaid whole-donation charge: `chargeWholeDonation` (lines 343-353) sums serializedByteCount over all blocks with overflow checks and does one `rateLimiter.tryConsume`. This applies only when job.blocks.count > 1 (line 276). If the charge is refused or the sum can't be computed, the code falls back to the original per-block charging (lines 302-309). So the endurance cap is not weakened. Total bytes charged equal the sum of per-block bytes, and blocks skipped after a successful charge stay charged (conservative). The prior ordering is preserved: low-disk guard and ENOSPC cooldown run before the charge, and the per-block file-access acquire and closed/cancel check run after it. The unsafe-URL path, the index-last ordering, the settlement callbacks (onBlockSettled via defer) and the outcome logic are unchanged.

One behavioral nuance: when the donation is prepaid, `rateLimited` can no longer be set mid-job, so a partial donation that hits write failures reports writeFailed rather than writeRateLimited. This is not security relevant. A side effect is that a prepaid charge for blocks later dropped (closed, safety check failed) is consumed. That is only a minor conservative endurance over-count, not a bypass of the T-041 endurance guard. No change to crypto, HMAC naming, TTL, at-rest metadata, or path safety (T-041 mitigations unchanged). The test file change is a comment-only edit. Remaining integration question: SSDWriteRateLimiter.tryConsume semantics (shared ledger, durable write) are outside the supplied evidence. Reducing ledger writes depends on that contract, and I saw no sign it affects confidentiality.
